correctness.rationale: Independent analytic reconstruction: orthogonality E χ²=1 verifies irreducibility of the two natural reflection representations (B_n all n≥1, D_n n≥3). The central convolution norm is degree times E|χ|. Derangement/fixed-point convolution, s_{2m} and s_{2m+1} signed-walk identities, ordinary/exponential generating functions, and a Bessel beta integral yield the exact alternating finite sum. Conditioning the even-sign subgroup only changes the identity-permutation case; its signed binomial sum gives the displayed parity defect, including the n=3 boundary. The strictly decreasing a_j proves the alternating limiting bound. A standalone exact enumeration verifies all signed-group character sums through rank 7 and further finite identities, explicitly not a proof at infinite ranks.

originality.rationale: Novelty claimed only for the exact uniform all-rank natural reflection-block endpoint norms and the B/D parity defect with Bessel limit, not for the standard character projector, irreducible representations, derangement enumeration, signed-walk moments, or Bessel integrals individually. Directly adjacent published framework arXiv:math/0701533 treats general projections and wreath-product representation decompositions, without the evaluated L1 character norm. Foata–Han q-basic signed-permutation generating functions are different statistics. Meaning-based published-finding corpus and literature searches for signed fixed-point character L1, type B/D reflections, equivalent wreath-product and Bessel formulations returned no dominating statement. Residual risk from unpublished/unindexed overlap and from full text of the Cambridge wreath-product monograph remains; absence of search hits is not proof of global novelty.

value.rationale: The reflection isotype is a canonical primitive Fourier block on two entire nonabelian Weyl-group families, not an arbitrary handpicked slice. Determining its exact endpoint amplification is a natural invariant. The all-rank type-B/D odd-rank coincidence, alternating even-rank index-two defect, and sharp explicit Bessel coefficient with strict remainder supply motivated structural information beyond reproducing a character table or a general projection formula. The group comparison cannot be obtained from the fixed-point statistics of the symmetric-group standard isotype alone.
